findings.title: environmental-monitoring TWA alert path fails open when reading timestamp is outside averaging window
findings.description: _calculate_twa always anchors the averaging window to datetime.now(), not the reading timestamp. record_reading accepts caller/sensor timestamps. For any TWA limit (noise 8h/0.25h, PM24h, CO 8h), if the reading's timestamp is older than averaging_period_hours, the filter yields no samples, _calculate_twa returns None, and _check_limits `continue`s without creating an alert — while the hazardous reading remains stored. Control with timestamp=now and value=100 dBA yields THRESHOLD_EXCEEDANCE against the 85 dBA OSHA TWA; the same 100 dBA with timestamp=now-10h yields zero alerts. Instantaneous limits (vibration/CO ceiling) still fire, proving the fail-open is specific to the TWA branch.
findings.impact: Delayed MQTT/backfill or attacker-spoofed timestamps suppress real-time OSHA/EPA exceedance alerts for noise and dust. Crews keep working under unsafe TWA conditions with a silent monitor.
attack_path: Add station monitoring ParameterType.NOISE (or PM10/CO TWA).
Ingest reading value=100 dBA (or equivalent exceedance) with timestamp older than the limit's averaging_period_hours (e.g. now-10h for noise).
_check_limits → _calculate_twa → None → continue; alerts list stays empty.
Dashboard consumers see no THRESHOLD_EXCEEDANCE → work proceeds.
Contrast: same value with timestamp=now creates exceedance alert immediately.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Distinct from already-reported (1) _get_compliance_status TWA-only display COMPLIANT and (2) WARNING suppressing later EXCEEDANCE for 1 hour. This is the alert-generation TWA branch failing open on empty windows via now()-anchored cutoff / backdated or delayed timestamps.
key_snippets: PoC: control now@100dBA → exceedance; attack now-10h@100dBA → 0 alerts

findings.title: defect-detection-ai computes dimensions_mm then ignores them for severity → structural cracks rated MINOR
findings.description: When pixels_per_mm is supplied, detect() calculates dimensions_mm from the bbox but severity is assigned solely by _classify_severity using bbox.area/image_area ratios (e.g. crack critical only if ratio≥0.10). A 100mm×10mm structural crack (far beyond ACI 224R 1mm critical width) occupying ~0.03% of a 4000×3000 frame is stamped MINOR. _assess_overall_condition then returns 'Good - Minor issues only' and _generate_recommendations emits sealant guidance instead of structural-engineer assessment.
findings.impact: False-negative severity downgrade lets unsafe structural defects pass QC as minor cosmetic issues → cover-up/continue work without engineering hold.
attack_path: Capture wide-field photo of a wide crack (or supply pixels_per_mm so physical size is large while bbox/image ratio stays <0.02).
DefectDetectionModel.detect(..., pixels_per_mm=2.0) stores dimensions_mm=(100,10) but severity=MINOR from ratio.
DefectInspectionSystem overall_condition='Good - Minor issues only'; recommendations='Seal minor crack(s)'.
QC/closeout treats element as acceptable to proceed.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Prior discard was SimpleDefectClassifier severity-from-confidence heuristic. This is the production DefectDetectionModel path that computes physical scale then ignores it for the severity SoR driving condition/recommendations.
key_snippets: Seal {len(group)} minor crack(s) with appropriate sealant.
